epidemic: An epidemic is a widespread illness, this spreads quickly to many people.
epigram: An epigram is a short (often two-line) poem which makes a point.
An epigram is a short, witty saying.
eponym: An eponym is something that is named after a person's name.
A spoonerism is an eponym, named after the Reverend William Archibald Spooner (1844–1930) who used to make the mistake when he spoke.
ephemeral: Something that is ephemeral is only temporary, it does not last long.
Here today and gone tomorrow" is a phrase which describes an ephemeral situation.
episode: An episode is an event or a short period of time that is important or unusual.
She remembered an especially strange episode that occurred when she was a teenager.
An episode is a part of a dramatic work such as a television or radio program.
This television series has 10 episodes and will be shown over the next 10 weeks.
ephebo: An ephebo is an adult who is sexually attracted to adolescents.
epitome: An epitome is a perfect example of something.
She is the epitome of elegance and beauty.
An epitome is a brief summary of a text.
ephebophilia: Ephebophilia is an adult's sexual attraction to a post-pubescent in their mid-late adolescence, usually between their 15-16 and 18-19 years, depending on the sex.
ephebophilic: If something is ephebophilic, it is related to ephebophilia.
ephebophile: An ephebophile is an adult who is sexually attracted to post-pubescents.
epoch: An epoch is a period of history made important by certain events.
epigraphy: Epigraphy is the study of ancient writings on a stone or other surface.
epigraphist: An epigraphist is a person who studies ancient writings on a stone or other surface.
epaulette: An epaulette is an ornamentation that is worn on the shoulders of a military uniform, as a sign of rank.
epistaxis: Epistaxis is bleeding from the nose.
Hypertension may contribute to epistaxis in some patients.
epiphany: An epiphany is a moment of sudden realization or discovery.
epidermis: The epidermis is the outer, protective layer of the skin of vertebrates.
The epidermis is the outer layer of cells in invertebrates and plants.
epitomize: If something epitomizes, it becomes an epitome.
epitomise: If something epitomises, it becomes an epitome.
epilepsy: Epilepsy is a medical condition in which a person experiences seizures and blackouts.
epistolary: If something is epistolary, it is related to letters, or the writing of letters.
eponymous: Something in a work that is eponymous shares a name with the work's title.
eproctophilia: Eproctophilia is a strong sexual interest in farts.
James Joyce showed eproctophilia in his 1909 letters by writing how he loved Nora’s farts.
epiphenomenalism: Epiphenomenalism is the idea that consciousness is created by the body and it does not do anything after its effect, to include making other thoughts.
epidemiology: Epidemiology is the study of how diseases and health conditions spread, occur, and affect groups of people.
epoxy: An epoxy is a strong adhesive or resin that hardens when mixed with a hardener, often used for bonding, coating, or sealing materials.
If you epoxy something, you glue, coat, or seal something using epoxy resin.
